+title: Delete the nested IntegrationTests package and update CI
+---
+## What
+
+`IntegrationTests/` is the gated real-model suite. It exists only to drive a live Router, and its 439-line `RouterIntegrationTests.swift` imports `FoundationModelsRouter` directly. Delete the package and the CI wiring that points at it.
+
+Files to change:
+- `IntegrationTests/` — delete the whole directory: `Package.swift` (106 lines), `Tests/FoundationModelsMetadataRegistryIntegrationTests/RouterIntegrationTests.swift` (439 lines), and `Support/MetalLibraryTestBootstrap.swift`.
+- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — delete the `integration-package-path: IntegrationTests` and `integration-metallib-glob: "*Cmlx*/default.metallib"` inputs. The `uses:` call to the shared `swift-ci.yaml` stays. Rewrite the header comment, which describes the nested package at length.
+- `Tests/FoundationModelsMetadataRegistryTests/CIWorkflowTests.swift` — delete `namesTheNestedIntegrationPackage()` (line 35) and `setsAMetallibGlob()` (line 50). Keep `callsTheSharedWorkflow()` (line 22). Rewrite the suite doc comment.
+
+Also delete the `SemanticSearchCore` library product in `Package.swift` (line 204-207) if nothing else needs it. It is a product only so the nested package could import it. Check first: the root test target reaches `SemanticSearchCore` as a target, not a product, so the product is probably now unused.
+
+### Open point for the user
+
+This removes every real-model test from the repository. The org test contract in swissarmyhammer/workflows' README is what the deleted CI inputs satisfy. Confirm the contract allows a repository with unit tests only before this task lands.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] `IntegrationTests/` does not exist.
+- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` sets no `integration-*` input and still calls the shared `swift-ci.yaml`.
+- [ ] No file in the repository imports `FoundationModelsRouter` except `Package.swift`.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsMetadataRegistryTests/CIWorkflowTests.swift` — `callsTheSharedWorkflow()` passes unchanged. Add a test that asserts `ci.yml` contains no line starting with `integration-`.
+- [ ] Run `swift test`. All tests pass.
+- [ ] Confirm `swift build --package-path IntegrationTests` now fails because the path does not exist, and that no script or workflow still runs it.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file

+  text: |
+    ### Validator rules read in full, and what they demanded
+
+    Loaded all 55 rules across the 7 validators matching `.swift`/`.yml`. Three bore on this change.
+
+    **1. `test-integrity / test-partitioning` check 4 — the rule this change is most exposed to.**
+
+    Its words: *"A test target that CI does not run — a CI workflow change that removes or omits a unit or integration test target... Each unit target and each integration target must appear in a CI task."* The rule carries no explicit carve-out for a target deleted in the same change, so the defence must be stated plainly rather than assumed:
+
+    - The `IntegrationTests` package no longer exists, so there is no target for CI to omit. The deletion and the CI-input removal land in the same change; CI never points at a target that is missing.
+    - `swift package describe` now reports exactly one test target, `Tests/FoundationModelsMetadataRegistryTests`, and the shared workflow's unit job runs it.
+    - Check 3 ("an integration test inside the unit target") was checked, not assumed: no test migrated into the unit target. Nothing in the root suite touches a network, a database, a spawned server, or a real model — every path runs on `DeterministicEmbedder`/`DemoAgentSession`, and the whole 109-test run finishes in 0.30s.
+    - This rule is also the SOURCE of the `IntegrationTests/` convention being removed. That is why the org contract was verified first (see the first comment): every `swift-ci.yaml` input is optional and the integration job is gated, so a unit-tests-only caller is valid.
+
+    **2. `completeness / public-output-contract` check 6 — removing the `.library` product.**
+
+    *"A public declaration removed... Confirm the task asked for that API change."* The card asks for it in terms: *"Also delete the `SemanticSearchCore` library product in `Package.swift`."* Its stated exception applies. No caller was left behind — the only importer was the deleted nested package.
+
+    **3. `code-hygiene / dead-code-swift` — the second-order effect, checked rather than assumed.**
+
+    Deleting the product and the nested test package both remove callers from periphery's index, so live declarations could have started reporting as dead. Verified directly: built an index store (`swift build --build-system native --build-tests -Xswiftc -index-store-path ...`, the default build system writes to `.build/out` where periphery does not look) and ran periphery 3.8.0 with the rule's own flag set (`--retain-public --retain-objc-accessible --retain-swift-ui-previews --retain-codable-properties`, test target report-excluded). Result: **"No unused code detected."** No `// periphery:ignore` marker was needed anywhere.
+
+    ### A rule that changed the code: `completeness / case-sensitivity-coverage`
+
+    That rule fires on *"the diff itself adds or changes how a textual token is matched"* — which is exactly what the new test does with the token `integration-`. The first draft matched case-sensitively. GitHub Actions resolves a `with:` key against the called workflow's `inputs:` without regard to case, so `Integration-Package-Path:` would switch the integration job on while a case-sensitive read let it through. Fixed: the filter is now `$0.lowercased().hasPrefix("integration-")`, with the reason in a comment above it.
+
+    The rule also asks for *"one regression test [that] feeds the relevant non-canonical spelling"*. Rather than add a second test, the single test was proven against that spelling by mutation: appending `Integration-Package-Path: IntegrationTests` to `ci.yml` fails it with `found: ["Integration-Package-Path: IntegrationTests"]`, and the file was restored to green.
+
+    ### `no-test-cheating` — the two clauses the new test had to survive
+
+    - *"Tests can be deleted entirely if they are no longer relevant or valid."* — explicit permission for removing `namesTheNestedIntegrationPackage()` and `setsAMetallibGlob()`.
+    - *"Every test should be able to fail."* Proven twice, not asserted: it failed RED before `ci.yml` was touched, and it failed again on each of two post-hoc mutations (canonical and mixed-case spellings). It is not the trivial assertion of check 2.
+    - Check 4, *"a weakened assertion"*, does not apply. The new test is not a looser restatement of the deleted pair — it asserts the inverse claim, because the requirement inverted: the old tests demanded the integration inputs be present, this one demands they be absent.
+
+    ### Rules that explicitly do NOT apply
+
+    - Stale prose comments are not a defect under any rule. `no-commented-code`'s own standard: *"A block that reads as English is prose however much punctuation it carries."* Both completeness rules say to stay silent on *"a comment or doc edit."* The rewrites were still made, because a comment naming a directory that no longer exists is wrong regardless of whether a validator scores it.
+    - `missing-docs-swift` gates on `[open, public]`. The internal suite and its internal `@Test` need no `///`, matching every sibling in the file.
+    - `magic-numbers-swift` reads numeric literals only; the prompt-level rule's defect is *repetition*, and `"integration-"` is used once. Its carve-out — *"Genuinely one-off literals used exactly once in an obvious context"* — covers it.
+    - No Swift line-length rule exists; `swift/idioms` hands whitespace to `swift-format`.
+
+    ### Final verification
+
+    - `swift build --build-tests`: no errors. Two warnings, both proven pre-existing by rebuilding with HEAD's `Package.swift` and getting them byte-identical.
+    - `swift test`: **109 tests in 10 suites, all pass, 0.30s** (was 110; minus 2 obsolete, plus 1 new).
+    - `swift build --package-path IntegrationTests` fails with `chdir error: No such file or directory`.
+    - No file outside `.kanban`/`plan.md` names `IntegrationTests`, and nothing anywhere names `METADATA_REGISTRY_INTEGRATION_TESTS`.
